name: Market / Risk / Compliance Analysts in Parallel With a Synthesizing Parent (Strategy.PARALLEL)
query: For each new deal we need three independent analyses — market, risk and compliance — followed by one combined memo. They shouldn't wait on each other. Build this as a single Python agent I can invoke from our `deal_review` workflow, and tell me what it costs in LLM calls per deal.
expected_behavior: Step 1: Consult references/agent-sdks.md §6 (the `parallel` row: all children run at once as a `FORK_JOIN`, the parent synthesizes; the parent's model is inherited from the first child if omitted), references/agents.md §4, references/workflow-definition.md (`### AGENT`), references/optimization.md F1 and F10 (fan-out multiplies LLM spend and worker load), and examples/agent-deploy-and-invoke.md (`agent-fork-specialists.json` for the workflow-side alternative).
Step 2: Three children with unique names, `provider/model`, their own instructions and `max_turns`: `market_analyst`, `risk_analyst`, `compliance` (e.g. `max_turns=5` each).

Step 3: Parent: `analysis = Agent(name="deal_analysis", model="openai/gpt-4o-mini", instructions="Combine the three analyses into one memo.", agents=[market_analyst, risk_analyst, compliance], strategy=Strategy.PARALLEL, max_turns=3)`. Explain the compiled shape: a `FORK_JOIN` over three `SUB_WORKFLOW`s (one per child) followed by the parent's synthesis turn; note the parent's `model` is inherited from the first child if omitted, and set it explicitly anyway.

Step 4: Cost (F10): at least one LLM call per child plus the synthesis turn per deal, each child up to its own `max_turns` — so keep the fan-out fixed and small (three), bound every child, and set `max_turns` on the parent.

Step 5: Lifecycle: `runtime.run(analysis, prompt)` under `if __name__ == "__main__":`; `runtime.deploy(analysis)` in CI; `runtime.serve(analysis)` only if any child has `@tool` workers (state `requiredWorkers`). Never `conductor deploy`.

Step 6: `deal_review` gets one task: `{"type":"AGENT","inputParameters":{"agentType":"conductor","name":"deal_analysis","prompt":"${workflow.input.deal_summary}","maxDurationSeconds":1200}}`; read `${ref.output.text}` / `.output.output.result`. `agentType` is `conductor`, never `"parallel"`.

Step 7: Mention the workflow-side alternative — a `FORK_JOIN` over three separately deployed agents with a JOIN and a fourth `AGENT` task — and when it fits (the specialists already exist as deployed agents owned by other teams).
Step 8: Verify offline with `mock_run` + `assert_agent_ran("risk_analyst")` (or `expect(result).completed()`), and live with `conductor agent stream <id>` (`subagent_start` / `subagent_stop` events).
success_criteria: The parent uses `agents=[market_analyst, risk_analyst, compliance]` with `strategy=Strategy.PARALLEL` (or `"parallel"`)
States that PARALLEL compiles to a `FORK_JOIN` over the children (each a `SUB_WORKFLOW`) and that the parent synthesizes their outputs
Sets the parent's `model` explicitly in `provider/model` form (noting that an omitted parent model is inherited from the first child is a plus)
Every `model` is provider-qualified (`provider/model`); no bare model names
Each child has a unique `name` and its own `max_turns`; the parent has `max_turns` too
Shows cost/F10 awareness: fan-out multiplies LLM calls (at least one per child plus the synthesis turn) and the branch count is kept fixed and small
Deploys with `runtime.deploy(...)` — never `conductor deploy` — and states whether a `serve()` process is needed (`requiredWorkers`)
The `AGENT` task in `deal_review` uses `agentType: "conductor"` + `name: "deal_analysis"` + `prompt` with `maxDurationSeconds` — never `agentType: "parallel"` or a framework name
Mentions a workflow-side `FORK_JOIN` alternative (over separately deployed agents or LLM tasks) and when the SDK strategy is the better fit
